**Vancouver, British Columbia – Integra Resources Corp. (“Integra” or the “Company”) (TSXV: ITR; NYSE American: ITRG** ) is pleased to announce financial and operating results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (the “third quarter” or “Q3 2026”). The Company will host a conference call to discuss third quarter 2026 results on Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time / 8:00 AM Pacific Time (Vancouver) / 7:00 AM Pacific Standard Time.


*(All amounts expressed in United States (“U.S.”) dollars unless otherwise stated)*


Third Quarter 2026 Highlights:


- Mined 5.3 million tonnes of ore and 3.6 million tonnes of waste at a strip ratio of 0.68 at the Florida Canyon Mine (the “Florida Canyon Mine” or “Florida Canyon” or the “Mine”) for Q3 2026. As a result, the Company achieved record mining rates which averaged 97,428 tonnes per day (“tpd”) for the quarter, compared to 64,488 tpd in Q3 2025.
- In Q3 2026, Florida Canyon produced 17,652 gold ounces and sold 16,760 gold ounces at an average realized price of $4,272 per gold ounce, compared to 20,653 gold ounces produced and 20,265 gold ounces sold at an average realized price of $3,464 in Q3 2025.
- Quarterly revenue of $72.4 million in Q3 2026, compared to revenue of $70.7 million in Q3 2025.
- Mine operating earnings of $23.3 million in Q3 2026 were comparable to $28.6 million in Q3 2025.
- Q3 2026 adjusted earnings(1) of $12.8 million, or $0.06 per share, was comparable to the $16.3 million, or $0.10 per share recorded in Q3 2025.
- Q3 2026 net earnings of $12.9 million, or $0.06 earnings per share, compared to net loss of $8.2 million, or $0.05 loss per share recorded in Q3 2025.
- Cash costs(1) averaged $2,419 per gold ounce, within revised guidance, and mine-site all in sustaining costs(1) (“Mine-site AISC”) averaged $3,059 per gold ounce in Q3 2026, below revised guidance. Cash costs and mine-site AISC remain impacted by increased mined, stacked and processed tonnes to support production, increased royalties and excise taxes resulting from stronger-than-anticipated gold prices, and higher diesel fuel and explosive costs.
- Operating cash flow of $21.8 million in Q3 2026 decreased from $35.6 million in Q3 2025, largely due to a $15.3 million increase in cash used for working capital, primarily driven by a build-up of inventories.
- Free cash flow(1) was $11.1 million, or $0.05 per share, for Q3 2026, compared to $20.2 million, or $0.12 per share in Q3 2025, due to lower operating cash flow.
- Cash and cash equivalents was $119.5 million at September 30, 2026, an increase from $63.1 million at December 31, 2025 and benefitting from the $57.5 million bought deal public offering completed in Q1 2026 and free cash flow from Florida Canyon. An additional $5.3 million of restricted cash was returned to the Company this quarter due to a reduction in required cash collateral related to Florida Canyon’s surety bonds program.
- The Company completed 14,309 meters of drilling this quarter, totaling 31,364 meters year to date, with encouraging results from two near-mine targets. Drilling between the Radio Tower and Central Open Pits continue to delineate a compelling zone of gold mineralization immediately adjacent to existing infrastructure. In addition, initial drilling into the northern extension of the Madre Shear zone intersected gold mineralization along a previously untested structure.
- The DeLamar Project entered the National Environmental Policy Act (“NEPA”) environmental review process on May 29, 2026, with the United States Bureau of Land Management’s (the “BLM”) publishing of the Notice of Intent, and concluded the 30-day public scoping process in June 2026. The Company is now working closely with the BLM to provide all appropriate data to address comments received during the public scoping process and conduct environmental effects analysis. The DeLamar Project Environmental Impact Statement (“EIS”) and Record of Decision (“RoD”) are anticipated in the second half of 2027.
- Integra has appointed GenCap Mining Advisory (“GenCap”) to assist the Company in evaluating and structuring potential financing alternatives for the future development of DeLamar. The early initiation of this process is intended to allow Integra to evaluate multiple sources of capital and establish a financing strategy well in advance of a potential final investment decision.
- Continued engagement with stakeholders across Nevada, Idaho, and Oregon, including local communities, civic and non-profit organizations, government officials, and Tribal nations. Specific engagement at DeLamar during the quarter included the “Let’s Talk DeLamar” series of town hall meetings, designed to facilitate feedback on local priorities and operational considerations that fall outside the environmental analysis conducted through NEPA.
- Wildcat Exploration Plan of Operations (“EPO”), now fully approved, will provide greater flexibility for significantly expanded exploration and hydrogeological drilling campaigns. Exploration drilling was initiated in August 2026 to collect additional hydrogeological, geotechnical, and metallurgical data that will inform development of the Mine Plan of Operations.
- The Company is revising its 2026 production guidance at Florida Canyon from 70,000–75,000 ounces of gold to 59,000–62,000 ounces, because recent leaching rates have not kept pace with increased mining rates. To maintain effective blending and long-term heap leach pad performance, mining rates will be reduced for the remainder of the year. As the stripping campaign in the Central Pit is completed next year, access to higher-grade ore is expected to increase production.


(1)This is a non-GAAP financial measure, please refer to the “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” disclosure at the end of this news release and associated MD&A for a description and calculation of this measure.


**George Salamis, President, CEO and Director of Integra commented:**


“Florida Canyon delivered its second consecutive quarter of production growth in Q3, producing 17,652 ounces of gold. That is an increase of 8% from the second quarter and 40% from the first quarter of 2026, driven by record mining rates that averaged 97,428 tonnes per day and processed grades that steadily improved through the year. However, leaching has not kept pace with these higher mining rates and to protect long-term heap leach pad performance and maintain effective blending, we’re reducing mining rates for the rest of the year and revising our 2026 production guidance to 59,000 to 62,000 ounces. The ounces have been placed on the heap leach pad and reducing mining rates should stabilize leach rates as we move into the Central Pit next year, providing access to higher-grade ore that will support future production. We’re continuing to advance targeted investments in stripping and heap leach pad expansion to support a longer mine life and a stronger production profile. Exploration drilling has also identified multiple targets next to our existing open pits and infrastructure, with the potential to grow mineral resources and extend mine life in future studies.


With US$119.5 million in the treasury, we’re well funded to execute our strategic investments at Florida Canyon while advancing our development pipeline. At DeLamar, we’ve advanced through the public scoping period and are working closely with the BLM toward an anticipated Record of Decision in the second half of 2027. In parallel with the permitting process at DeLamar, we’ve engaged GenCap to evaluate financing alternatives well ahead of a potential construction decision. We’re also continuing our engagement with communities, Tribal nations and other stakeholders, including our ‘Let’s Talk DeLamar’ town halls. At Nevada North, we’re advancing resource conversion drilling, geotechnical work and permitting.”

**Florida Canyon Mine**


Mining


In Q3 2026, the Company mined 5.3M tonnes of ore, up 111% from 2.5M in Q3 2025, and 3.6M tonnes of waste, up 6% from 3.4M in Q3 2025 at a strip ratio of 0.68, 49% lower than 1.34 in Q3 2025. As a result, mining rates averaged 97,428 tpd compared to 64,488 tpd in Q3 2025, representing a record rate of total material movement at the Mine. This mining rate was achieved this quarter due to the new mining equipment integrated into the fleet over the previous two quarters and shorter haul distances.


Production


In Q3 2026, the Company produced 17,652 ounces of gold, compared to 20,653 ounces in Q3 2025.


Record mining rates this year have increased the ounces stacked on the heap leach pads, driving quarter-over-quarter production growth. A larger share of run-of-mine (“ROM”) ore was placed on the pads, which lowered the blended gold recovery rate because ROM ore is expected to recover less gold than crushed ore. The ore stacking and blending strategy used since Q1 is being monitored closely and refined at these higher mining rates to maintain production guidance.


Sustaining and Non-sustaining Capital


During Q3 2026, the Company invested $10.6 million in sustaining capital, compared to $15.4 million in Q3 2025. Spending in Q3 2026 reflects the Company’s continued reinvestment strategy including new mobile equipment leases and refurbishments, capital stripping and exploration drilling. The Company expects investments in sustaining capital expenditures to continue into the fourth quarter.


The Company also invested $1.3 million in Q3 2026, in non-sustaining growth capital, comparable to $1.8 million invested in the third quarter of 2025. This spending was primarily directed toward mobile equipment leases for the expanded fleet, engineering and permitting work on Phase 3C leach pad facility and growth-focused drilling programs at the Florida Canyon Mine discussed further in the Exploration section below.


Cash Costs and Mine-site AISC


Cash costs averaged $2,419 per ounce in Q3 2026 and Mine-site AISC averaged $3,059 per ounce in Q3 2026. These metrics were impacted by increased mined, stacked and processed tonnes to support production, increased royalties and excise taxes resulting from stronger-than-anticipated gold prices, and higher diesel fuel and explosive costs. See the Guidance Section below for further details on the 2026 revised guidance.


Royalties and excise taxes, which constitute a material component of cash costs and Mine-site AISC, are directly impacted by fluctuations in the gold price. The Company’s revised guidance assumed an average gold price of $4,200 per ounce, and a $100 per ounce change in the gold price results in an estimated $7 change to both cash costs and Mine-site AISC.


Florida Canyon Exploration


In Q3 2026, the Company completed 14,309 meters of drilling, totaling 31,364 meters year to date, of its 42,500 meter 2026 growth focused drilling program at Florida Canyon. The 2026 program continues on the success of the 2025 program focusing on four key areas: (1) Resource development at the Florida Canyon Mine Property; (2) underexplored extensions of Florida Canyon Gold mineralization exploration (3) Standard Mine area targets; and (4) greenfield exploration targets. The program is specifically designed to support resource and reserve growth and extend mine life at Florida Canyon.


Program expenditures, included in sustaining and non-sustaining capital, totaled $3.0 million in Q3 2026.


**Development Projects**


DeLamar capital and project expenses


In Q3 2026, the Company incurred $2.0 million in exploration and project expenses, largely for site general and administrative (“G&A”) and external affairs work. The completion of the 2,000 meter development drilling program is scheduled for early Q4 2026. In addition, the Company invested $7.6 million in mineral property, plant, and equipment at DeLamar, including $4.2 million in permitting and engineering activities, and $2.5 million in de-risking activities, of which $2.0 million was for securing equipment.


DeLamar permitting


Integra’s 2025 DeLamar Project Mine Plan of Operations (“MPO”) Version 4.3 was submitted to the BLM on May 1, 2026. The MPO Version 4.3 is the project proposed action and will serve as the basis for BLM’s environmental review of the DeLamar Project under the NEPA. The BLM’s NEPA process initiated with the publishing of the Notice of Intent (“NOI”) on May 29, 2026, initiating a 30-day public scoping process to identify environmental concerns (issues) associated with project implementation. Environmental effects analysis of the DeLamar Project and a no action alternative will be issued in an EIS and accompanying RoD, anticipated in H2 2027. In the EIS, the BLM will identify a preferred alternative and any required mitigation measures required for the DeLamar Project implementation. Following the NEPA process, a final revised MPO will be prepared that incorporates the preferred alternative and any identified mitigation measures. Once all applicable federal, state and local permits are obtained, the DeLamar Project will commence construction.


The DeLamar Project’s permitting timeline was posted to the FAST-41 project dashboard on January 13, 2026 and is available here: www.permits.performance.gov. The FAST-41 Transparency Project program is a federal permitting framework designed to streamline environmental reviews, improve interagency coordination, and increase transparency. Agencies must develop and maintain a coordinated, project-specific timetable for all required environmental review and permitting actions. Integra has been designated a dedicated project advisor from the Permitting Council, who monitors the advancement of the project and supports active engagement and coordination across multiple regulatory agencies. The Permitting Council provides high-level oversight to ensure that federal agencies adhere to established timetables. The DeLamar Project’s permitting timeline posted to the FAST-41 project dashboard highlights an accelerated 15-month NEPA schedule from start to finish.


The Company completed its feasibility study for the DeLamar Project with an effective date December 8, 2025. The feasibility study for DeLamar confirmed robust economics for a low-cost, large-scale, conventional open pit oxide heap leach operation, with competitive operating costs and a high rate of return. The feasibility study outlines total production of 1.1 million ounces of gold equivalent (“AuEq”) over a 10-year operating mine life (plus two years of residual leaching), resulting in an average annual production profile of 106,000 ounces AuEq per annum at a co-product Mine-site AISC of $1,480 per ounce (“/oz”) AuEq. Initial capital costs are $389 million, including $38 million of owners’ cost, and sustaining capital of $305 million over the mine life. The DeLamar Project generates an after-tax net present value (“NPV5%”) of approximately $774 million with an after-tax internal rate of return (“IRR”) of 46% at base case gold and silver prices of $3,000/oz and $35/oz, respectively. After-tax NPV5% improves to approximately $1.9 billion and after-tax IRR to 97% using recent gold and silver prices of $4,500/oz and $65/oz, respectively.


2026 Revised Guidance and Outlook


Based on recent operating performance, Integra is revising its 2026 gold production guidance at the Florida Canyon Mine from 70,000–75,000 ounces to 59,000–62,000 ounces.


This year, the Company increased mining and stacking rates at Florida Canyon to maintain production from lower-grade ore while stripping the Central Pit, the location of higher-grade ore that supports future production. Recent leaching rates have not kept pace with rate of mining and to maintain effective blending and long-term heap leach pad performance, the Company will reduce mining rates for the remainder of the year.


While the ounces have been stacked on the heap leach pads, slower leach rates have delayed their recovery. In 2027, mining will advance into higher-grade ore from the Central Pit, which is expected to support improved leach performance and gold production.

**Selected Q3 Financial Results**


Revenue


In Q3 2026 the Company sold 16,760 ounces of gold at average realized prices of $4,272 per ounce of gold generating revenue of $72.4 million, compared to 20,265 ounces at average realized prices of $3,464 per ounce in Q3 2025, resulting in revenues of $70.7 million.


Net Earnings


During the three months ended September 30, 2026, net earnings were $12.9 million compared to net loss of $8.2 million for the same period in 2025. The net earnings in Q3 2026 largely resulted from strong mine operating earnings supported by strong average realized gold prices, while the net loss in the comparable period was primarily driven by $17.7 million of non-cash unrealized derivative loss on the conversion feature of the convertible debt facility.


Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $12.8 million, or $0.06 per share, was lower than adjusted earnings of $16.3 million or $0.10 per share in Q3 2025, primarily driven by higher costs of sales due largely to increased diesel fuel and explosive costs.


Cash Flow


Cash flows provided by operations in Q3 2026 totaled $21.8 million, a decrease of $13.8 million compared to the $35.6 million generated in Q3 2025. The primary driver of this decrease is related to a $15.3 million decrease in working capital cash inflow, largely driven by a buildup of inventories.


During the third quarter, the Company made payments of $19.5 million for mineral properties, plant and equipment, and leases. This increased from payments of $17.4 million for mineral property, plant and equipment, and leases made in Q3 2025, which were related to sustaining capital expenditures at Florida Canyon and capitalized development costs at DeLamar.


Q3 2026 free cash flow generated of $11.1 million, or $0.05 per share, compared to $20.2 million, or $0.12 per share, generated in Q3 2025.


Financial Position


As at September 30, 2026, the Company had a cash and cash equivalent balance of $119.5 million, an increase of $56.4 million from $63.1 million at December 31, 2025.


The Company’s working capital was $159.5 million on September 30, 2026, reflecting a $66.6 million increase from December 31, 2025. This improvement was largely attributable to a $56.4 million increase in cash, benefiting from the $57.5 million bought deal public offering and an additional $5.3 million of restricted cash was returned to the Company this quarter due to a change in surety bond provider.


Health, Safety and Environment


Integra experienced zero fatalities and one lost time injury (two year-to-date) in Q3 2026. Including the lost time injury, two MSHA-reportable injuries occurred at Florida Canyon in Q3 2026 (five year-to-date). The 2026, year-to-date total reportable incident frequency rate (“TRIFR”) at Florida Canyon was 1.7 compared to 2.4 for YTD 2025. ****


Integra experienced zero quarterly reportable spills (one year-to-date), zero immediately reportable spills (zero year-to-date) and one minor reportable permit noncompliance for the quarter (three year-to-date), all at Florida Canyon.
